cards.explanation: The answer is that Ahimelech wants to know why David is alone. Ahimelech, the priest at Nob, trembles and asks David, “Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?” (1 Samuel 21:1). I can picture it. David walks in, and the shaking priest asks about the empty space behind him. He skips the small talk and goes straight to the question.

The answer is True. David tells Ahimelech, “The king has given me a mission…” and adds that the king told him no one is to know about it (1 Samuel 21:2). So David gives the priest his reason in one tidy package, like a lid on a cookie jar.

The answer is consecrated. Ahimelech says, “There is no common bread on hand, but there is some consecrated bread” (1 Samuel 21:4). Consecrated means set apart as holy. Verse 6 says it was the Bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD. That's not the sort of bread you grab on a lunch run.

The answer is True. David tells Ahimelech, “Women have indeed been kept from us, as is usual when I set out.” (1 Samuel 21:5). He adds that the bodies of the young men are holy even on common missions. Ahimelech had set one condition, and David says it's met.

The answer is shepherd and Saul. The text calls Doeg the Edomite “…the chief shepherd for Saul.” (1 Samuel 21:7). He's Saul's top man over the shepherds, and Saul is the king David fled from. The text also says Doeg was “…detained before the LORD.” at Nob that day, and it says no more than that. So one of Saul's own servants is at Nob that day, and I think that's worth noticing, friends.

The answer is a spear or a sword. David asks, “Is there not a spear or sword on hand here?” (1 Samuel 21:8). He says he brought neither his sword nor his weapons, because the king's mission was urgent. First bread, now a weapon. Friends, that's a man asking for supplies one question at a time.

The answer is Goliath. Ahimelech says, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here…” (1 Samuel 21:9). It's wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. David killed the man, and now his sword is sitting there wrapped up like a keepsake.

The answer is False. David takes the sword. He says, “There is none like it; give it to me.” (1 Samuel 21:9). Ahimelech had told him, “For there is no other but this one here.” I think David isn't wasting a second on that one.

The answer is Achish king of Gath. That day David “…fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.” (1 Samuel 21:10). Gath was a Philistine city, and Goliath the Philistine had come from Gath (1 Samuel 17:4). So David has the sword of Goliath, and he's walking into the giant's hometown. Friends, that's one bold detour.

The answer is that Saul killed thousands and David tens of thousands. The servants of Achish say, “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands…” (1 Samuel 21:11). They remember it as a song sung in their dances. Imagine your hit single coming back at you in Gath, friends.

The answer is that David pretends to be insane. David “…changed his behavior before them and feigned madness in their hands…” (1 Samuel 21:13). He's very much afraid of Achish, so he plays the madman. I think it was a big risk.

The answer is that Achish says the man is insane, so why bring him. Achish tells his servants, “Look, you can see that the man is insane! Why have you brought him to me?” (1 Samuel 21:14). He goes on, “Must this man come into my house?” (1 Samuel 21:15). So the act is working. I think Achish sounds more annoyed than alarmed.
